comparison: Three identical fictional needs and corpus hashes; one observed call per version per case. Versions differ in concise candidate instructions and intake effort. This does not isolate either change or establish general model accuracy.

cases.need: The Budget Office has a working application and an already approved Colorado Azure target environment. Our release manager owns deployment. We have a repeatable build and the application source. We need a managed source repository, automatic build and test checks, security scans, release approval and a record of deployments. We do not need a new hosting environment or identity project. Success is deploying a reviewed build to the approved environment and identifying which version is running.
cases.expect: Delivery-pipeline offering is a whole-need fit. Do not prefer a broad new environment project; routine provisioning is a condition, not invented missing capability.

cases.need: Our field teams record landslide observations where there is no network. They record rock type, GPS coordinates and condition in writing; no photographs are needed. Replace the paper form with fully offline capture and sync when they return. Other teams need a shared page filtered by site and date, available by the following morning. We have no existing record system. OIT will need to help us work out that part.
cases.expect: Useful offline capture component may be reviewer evidence. No requester suggestion for an unverified capture-to-viewer chain. Preserve offline and next-morning requirements.

cases.need: We need laboratory equipment that measures the isotope ratios in rock samples using laser-ablation mass spectrometry. The purpose is to measure the chemical composition of the physical samples, not to store documents, create maps, track a workflow or build an analysis dashboard. Success is a calibrated physical measurement with laboratory traceability. A database or map cannot perform the measurement.
cases.expect: No requester suggestion and no asset or service pretending to perform the measurement; physical equipment need preserved.

observations: Both versions selected the delivery-pipeline service for the clear-release need and withheld requester suggestions for the partial-field and no-fit needs.
Offline capture, no photographs, and next-morning shared access survived in the updated requirements. The no-fit case retained physical measurement and returned empty matching lists.

The updated field asset calls unused photograph capture a gap even though the text itself says it is not a problem. Both versions retained a weak, overbroad deployment service in reviewer evidence. Those explanations require reviewer judgment; they are not verified facts or routing decisions.
The updated version asked additional questions in cases where the baseline asked none. Fewer tokens or shorter latency does not establish lower user effort.
No request submission or satisfaction rating was produced. Real paid receipts remain in the normal application ledger.
